newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down on dlr short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down on dlr short-covering.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed lower at 26.355 on Thursday from 26.353 as banks covered dollars they shorted yesterday, dealers said.
Banks decided to buy dollars again after the Central Bank bought about $49 million yesterday. Banks had been selling dollars because of rising domestic interest rates.

But the dollar buying was restrained because of expectations of higher interest rates after the Central Bank raised on Thursday its six-month reverse repo rate to 10.5625 from 10.25 percent, dealers said.
Banks also remain wary in case liquidity tightens next week when banks remit income tax payments to the government early next week, they said.
The Central Bank stayed out of the market, dealers said.
Turnover thinned to $90.5 million from $201.6 million.
